title: Junkstronaut game parameters
description: The Economy Balancer's output, and the crew's headline artifact. This is the object that becomes config/game_params.tres — the one file the game loads and the only place a tunable value may live.

ablation.description: The model is stated in the Economy Balancer's charter and is the single definition the game, the audit and the report all use. A descent is k shallow skims followed by one committed entry, so k+1 heat cycles: cost(band,k) = SUM(i=0..k) cycle_toll_base_pct * cycle_toll_growth^i + heat_cost_coefficient * (heat_index[band] * skim_heat_multiplier[k])^heat_cost_exponent + k * heat_cost_coefficient * skim_peak^heat_cost_exponent. cost_curve is the Balancer's own evaluation of it, so nothing downstream reconstructs the model from prose. This replaces an earlier model that divided peak heat by pass count; flying it showed a committed entry's peak is set by entry depth and ballistic coefficient, not by how many passes preceded it.

cycle_toll_base_pct.description: Thermal-fatigue toll for the first heat cycle, in percent of plate.

cycle_toll_growth.description: Multiplier applied per subsequent cycle. Must exceed 1: a flat toll is linear in skim count and cannot hold the optimum in place.

skim_peak.description: Peak heat of one shallow skim pass on the 0-100 bar. Skims are cool; the committed entry dominates.

skim_heat_multiplier.description: Factor on the committed entry's peak after 0, 1, 2 and 3 skims. Starts at 1.0, non-increasing, floored at 0.15 — skimming cools the entry but the benefit saturates once the orbit is grazing. The floor was 0.4, chosen before the simulator could measure this quantity properly; with the skim altitude scanned rather than hardcoded, 13% of sampled grid worlds measure below 0.4 and the lowest reads 0.277. A floor above what the flight model actually produces is worse than no floor: the Auditor's instruction to adopt the measured values would be unsatisfiable, and the Balancer would fail its schema three times and kill the run rather than report the problem.

heat_index.description: Peak heat of a DIRECT entry from each band, no skims, on the 0-100 heat bar.

cost_curve.description: Plate burned for 0..3 skims, per band. Exactly four numbers each, in skim order.

optimal_skims.description: 0-based index of each cost_curve's minimum. The high band must be 1 or 2, and no band may exceed it, so the return leg gets harder with altitude.

landing.description: The canopy is stated, not implied. parachute_area_m2 and parachute_drag_coefficient are required because without them the simulator had to solve the area backwards from descent_speed_full_hold_ms and then measure that same speed — a check of the claim against itself. With both stated, the descent is flown from the physical canopy and descent_speed_full_hold_ms becomes a prediction the flight can contradict.

parachute_area_m2.description: Canopy reference area. The simulator flies this; it does not infer it.

parachute_drag_coefficient.description: Canopy drag coefficient. Required alongside the area so the terminal velocity is fully determined by the params rather than by a default living in the model.

descent_speed_full_hold_ms.description: Predicted touchdown speed at base storage with a full hold. The Auditor flies the stated canopy and fails this if the measurement disagrees, so it is a claim about the flight and not a target the area was fitted to.

catalog_concerns.description: The Balancer's channel for reporting a problem in the debris catalog it was given. It may never re-author the catalog itself — a second copy of the loot table is two sources of truth, and the fix silently reverts the moment anyone reads the original. Raising a concern here routes the finding to the Debris Designer, which is the agent that owns that data.
